notes: The earlier required change is resolved. close_up_whitespace (compiler.py:1475-1496) is back to collapsing only [ \t]{2,} runs and trailing spaces before a newline. The new test shows 'Lord ; and . . . then', French 'mot : suite' and an NBSP before ':' all come through unchanged.

The cleanup now happens only where a removed false scope is joined to the text before it. _handle_conditional_element resets _omitted_conditional_end each time it is called (compiler.py:1131). It records the closer only when the scope it pops was FALSE when the opener was evaluated (1178-1180), and never evaluates the condition again at the closer. _prefix_before_tail acts only when child is that same element (an lxml proxy, kept alive by the reference held), and clears it once used. The attribute is set to None in __init__ (207), so a dropped settings element or comment can't raise AttributeError. If state is left over, for example a false closer with no tail, nothing goes wrong, because the identity check can only match that closer. No cached source XML is changed: only output text and tails are rewritten.

Inside nested false scopes, the inner closer is recorded, but _carry_dropped_tail and the inline tail branch both return early while the outer scope is still on the stack. The outer closer's own call to _handle_conditional_element then resets and sets the state again. This is correct.

whitespace.prefix_after_omission removes trailing [ \t\r\n] only when the closer's tail begins with closing punctuation for the language (French: only , . ׃). It never fires if the tail begins with whitespace (a space the source prints before the punctuation is kept), with '. .' or '..' (ellipses), or after NBSP or U+202F, which the regex does not match. Language comes from the closer's parent in the source, which is correct. The punctuation list is conservative: ')', ']', '…' and closing quotes are not included, so the source spacing before them stays. That is the safe choice.
The inline compiler uses the same helper at the same point, and the test covers all three processors × false/true/undefined × six spacing cases, including the newline-and-indent wrap.

markers._conditional_separators now treats newlines as separators and uses the same closes_omitted_insert test, so spaced ellipses and French spacing get no separator scope (as the test shows). The seg is inserted before the marked opener, so the brackets and the text they enclose are unchanged. It runs before _number_scopes, so the copy keeps p:pinned and gets the same expression index.

In the XSLT, the cheap exists(...) test now runs before f:sets-text. Marked openers and all closers keep the lb, so a ']' on a line of its own does not run into the next verse. Explicit layout elements and p:part='last' keep it too. A line holding only a silent marker gets no empty row, which is what was intended.
No source readings or canonical identities are touched by this code.
